# NanoFlow AI Retrieval Guide

NanoFlow is an offline-first personal task workflow PWA. Use this file as the entry point for AI assistants and Context7-style retrievers.

## Non-Negotiable Rules

- Entity IDs are client-generated strings. New entities use `crypto.randomUUID()`.
- Writes are local-first and non-blocking. Failed remote writes enter retry queues.
- Last-Write-Wins uses `updatedAt` / `updated_at`.
- Soft deletes use `deletedAt` / `deleted_at`; tombstones must not be dropped casually.
- Task sync queries must include `content`.
- Angular Signals are the state baseline. Do not add global facade stores.
- Mobile uses Text view by default. GoJS Flow is lazy and must not remain alive under `visibility:hidden`.
- Secrets belong in Supabase Secrets or deployment environment variables, not frontend code.

## Context7 Indexing Intent

`context7.json` intentionally indexes only `docs/context7`. The rest of the repository contains source code, tests, generated output, archives, and long historical plans that are useful for development but noisy for external AI retrieval.

## Live Consistency Intent

When source, configuration, schema, migration, Supabase function, sync, security, or UI lifecycle behavior changes, the same change must update the relevant Context7 page. `npm run docs:context7:guard` enforces this by combining the structural validator with `scripts/contracts/check-context7-coupled-changes.cjs`.
